claude.performance_metric: Resold ~48 months after go-private for ~$8.5bn vs ~$5.0-5.5bn paid (2017), described as "a healthy return"
claude.rationale: The realized record documents a continuing operating business at broadly similar scale (18,000+ colleagues, trials in 95+ countries) and a profitable resale to EQT/Goldman Sachs in 2021, with no documented product/operations incoherence — so p4_pathway is 0. Likewise, no documented operations-vs-organization fracture appears: the only personnel event is a pre-window CEO succession (founder von Rickenbach stepping down in March 2018), with Macdonald continuing to lead through the 2021 close, and no evidence of integration breaking against people/management/culture — so p5_pathway is 0. No archetype incoherence or business-model incompatibility is documented in the slice.

gemini.rationale: The slice documents that PAREXEL operated successfully under private ownership, adapting to the pandemic and maintaining over 18,000 employees. There is no documented evidence of product/process disruption (p4_pathway = 0) or process/organization fracture (p5_pathway = 0), as the company was ultimately sold for approximately $8.5 billion in 2021, representing a healthy return for the initial acquirer.

grok.rationale: The slice documents no product/process interface disruption: within the 2020-2022 window PAREXEL continued at broadly similar scale (18,000+ colleagues; trials in 95+ countries) and was resold intact for ~$8.5bn. No process/organization fracture is documented either; the only leadership change noted is a pre-window founder-CEO succession (2018), after which the company operated under continuing CEO Jamie Macdonald through the completed 2021 change-of-control with the existing executive team retained. Absence of any realized disruption evidence codes both pathways 0.
